verdict.rationale: Better Auth's own docs say it supports multiple built-in social providers (Google, GitHub, Apple, Discord, and more), and its SSO plugin adds generic OIDC, OAuth2 and SAML 2.0 providers. A community user confirms using the built-in Google, Apple and GitHub providers, and another reports many sign-in options from included plugins and defaults without writing special code. However, the pack shows no social-provider configuration snippet and never lists the full set of providers, so the 'configuration, not custom code' and 'broad set' parts are only implied. Missing for 10: a documented socialProviders configuration example showing providers enabled purely by config, an enumerated count or list of supported providers beyond 'and more', and independent hands-on confirmation of generic OAuth/OIDC setup via configuration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can offer sign-in with a broad set of social and OAuth identity providers through configuration, not custom code

citations.quote: Better Auth supports multiple social providers, including Google, GitHub, Apple, Discord, and more.
This plugin supports OpenID Connect (OIDC), OAuth2 providers, and SAML 2.0.
They use the built-in OAuth providers for Google, Apple and GitHub logins.
gets all of this from included plugins and defaults, without writing a single line of special code
